the long-term treatment with the PPAR pan-agonist TTA or with FO was associated with changes in the cardiac FA composition and cardiac lipid metabolism.

long-term treatment with the PPAR-agonist tetradecytlthioacetic or fish oil is accompanied by increased cardiac content of the n-3 fatty acid, docosahexaenoic acid, and increased expression of the genes for fatty acid oxidation and uncoupling protein 3.
long-term administration of TTA or FO is associated with increased n-3 PUFAs and increased FA oxidation in the heart.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of long-term treatment with a pan-PPAR-activating fatty acid, TTA, and a natural n-3 PUFO, FO, on cardiac lipid metabolism.
the long-term effects on cardiac lipid metabolism of the pan- PPAR agonist TTA and/or high-doses of FO.
the effects of long-term administration of the pan- PPAR agonist TTA, and/or fish oil (FO), on cardiac and liver fatty acid composition, and on cardiac and liver lipid metabolism in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the long-term treatment with TTA or FO is associated with a marked increase in the content of n- 3 fatty acids in the heart, which may have implications for the treatment of patients with heart disease.
TTA and FO supplementation are associated with increased cardiac n-3 fatty acid content.
the TTA and FO treatments induced different but not opposite effects on cardiac FA metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the long-term treatment with the PPAR-α agonist TTA and FO are associated with increased cardiac levels of n-3 PUFAs and a selective increase of Ucp3 and Pgc-1α in the heart.
the long-term treatment with TTA and/or FO induced marked changes on the cardiac fatty acid composition and enzymatic activities involved in FA metabolism.
TTA and/or FO may be beneficial to cardiac function and metabolism in the long-term, but the underlying mechanisms remain to be elucidated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long-term treatment with the PPAR agonist TTA is associated with an increase in the cardiac levels of n-3 PUFAs, which may have beneficial effects on cardiac metabolism.
TTA or FO treatment is associated with a selective increase in n-3 PUFAs in the heart and that these changes are accompanied by an increased activity of enzymes involved in FA metabolism.
the long-term effects on the heart are different from the liver, and that the effects of TTA and FO on the heart are additive.
